chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I hired a mule to Qasr Ibn Hubeyra, going and coming, for such and such (amount), and I went out in seeking the debt for me. So when I got near to the arch of Al Kufa, I was informed that my companion had gone to the Nile. So I diverted towards the Nile. So when I got to the Nile, I was informed that my companion had gone to Baghdad. So I pursued him, and I was successful with it, and I was free from what was between me and him, and we returned to Al Kufa, and the going and coming was of (a duration of) fifteen days.

So I informed my companion with my excuse, and I wanted to release myself from him from what I had done and to please him, so I offered him fifteen Dirhams. But he refused to accept. So we both agreed with (going to) Abu Hanifa. So I informed him with the story and the man informed him of it. So he said to me, 'And what did you do with the mule?' So I said, 'I have handed it over to him, safely.' He said, 'Yes, after fifteen days!' So he (Abu Hanifa) said, 'And what do you want with the man?' He said, 'I want the hire charges for my mule withheld from me for fifteen days.' So he said, 'I do not see for you a right, because he had hired it to Qasr Ibn Hubeyra, so he differed and rode it to the Nile, and to Baghdad. So he is responsible for the price of the mule and the hire charges are dropped. So when he returned the mule safely and you took possession of it, the hire charges are not obligated upon him.'

He said, 'So we came out from his presence and the owner of the mule went on to say 'We are from Allah and to Him we are returning', due to what Fatwa Abu Hanifa had issued with. So I gave him something, and freed myself from him. Then I went on Hajj during that year. So I informed Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) with what Fatwa Abu Hanifa had issued with. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is due to these (types of) judgements and what resembles these that the sky withholds its water and the earth prevents its Blessings'.

He said, 'So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'So what is your view?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I view for him, upon you, similar hire charges of a mule going from Al Kufa to the Nile, and similar hire charges of a mule riding from the Nile to Baghdad, and a similar hire charges of a mule from Baghdad to Al Kufa. Pay it to him'.

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I had fed it with Dirhams, so for me, upon him, would be its feeding (to reduce from the hire charges).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because you are a usurper'.

I said, 'What is your view, if the mule had been injured and died, would not that have been obligated upon me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, a price of a mule on the day you opposed him'. I said, 'Supposing the mule had been affected by a fracture, or injury, or disease?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon you would be its price what is between the healthy and the faulty on the day you returned it to him'. I said, 'And who would recognise that (difference)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You and him, and either he swears an oath upon the price, so it would be necessitated upon you. So if he were to return the swearing of the oath upon you, and you swear upon the price, that would necessitate upon him, or else the owner of the mule would come with witnesses who would be testifying that the price of the mule when it was hire was such and such, so it would be necessitated upon you'.

I said, 'I had given him some Dirhams and pleased him with it, and he freed me'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'But rather, he was pleased with it and freed you when Abu Hanifa judged against him with the inequity and the injustice, but return to him and inform him with what Fatwa I have issued with. So if he were to make you to be free after recognising it, so there would not be anything upon you after that'.

Abu Wallad said, 'So when I left from that direction of mine to meet the hirer, I informed him with what Fatwa Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) had issued to me with, and I said to him, 'Say whatever you so desire to and I shall give it to you'. So he said, 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) has become beloved to me and there has occurred the preference for him in my heart, and you are free, and if you so like that I return to you that which I have taken from you, I would do so'.

key_terms.قِيمَةُ مَا بَيْنَ الصِّحَّةِ وَ الْعَيْ: the difference in value between healthy and defective

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Abu Hanifa's and Imam al-Sadiq's ruling on hiring an animal and deviating from the agreed route?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the jurisprudential divergence between the Hanafi school and the Ahl al-Bayt regarding *ikra* (animal hire) when the hirer deviates from the agreed route. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that deviation constitutes usurpation (*ghasb*) of the animal's utility, thereby obligating payment for the actual time and distance used, while also clarifying that subsequent acceptance by the owner does not validate the initial unjust ruling if the owner was unaware of the deviation's legal implications. The narrative highlights the Shia principle that justice requires compensating for actual benefit derived rather than voiding the contract entirely, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic emphasis on fulfilling trusts and avoiding oppression.
